The simulation uses twoPhaseEulerFoam to model incompressible, isothermal, two-phase (oil-water) flow in a horizontal pipe.
The pipe has a circular cross-section with diameter D = 0.05 m and length L = 1 m, oriented along the x-axis.
Gravity is set to (0 -9.81 0) m/s² in constant/g to account for phase separation in the horizontal pipe.
The mesh resolves the pipe cross-section with at least 20 cells across the diameter; a blockMesh-based cylindrical or hexahedral decomposition of the circular domain is used with sufficient axial cells (e.g., 100+ along the length).
The water phase has density 1000 kg/m³ and dynamic viscosity 0.001 Pa·s.
The oil phase has density 850 kg/m³ and dynamic viscosity 0.001 Pa·s.
These properties are defined in constant/transportProperties using Newtonian type entries for each phase.
The inlet boundary condition for U is fixedValue with uniform (0.3 0 0), imposing a mixture velocity of 0.3 m/s in the pipe axis direction.
The inlet boundary condition for alpha.water is fixedValue with uniform 0.3.
The inlet boundary condition for p (or p_rgh) is zeroGradient.
The outlet boundary condition for alpha.water is zeroGradient.
The outlet boundary condition for U is inletOutlet.
The outlet boundary condition for p (or p_rgh) is fixedValue with uniform 0.
All wall boundaries use noSlip for U, zeroGradient for alpha.water, and fixedValue uniform 0 for p (or p_rgh).
The case is run in transient mode with a sufficiently small time step (e.g., deltaT = 0.001 s) and is considered to have reached steady state when the maximum change in alpha.water and U between successive iterations falls below a tolerance of 1e-4 over 100+ time steps.
The controlDict uses steadyState or a long-enough endTime to allow the transient solution to converge to a time-independent profile.
All chosen default values (D, L, mixture velocity, fluid properties, time step) are documented in the case description file.
